newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Antwerp seaport traffic fell 1.4 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Antwerp seaport traffic fell 1.4 pct in 1996.

text.p: The Belgian seaport of Antwerp, one of Europe's biggest, said on Monday that total traffic slipped by 1.4 percent to 106.53 million tonnes in 1996, mainly due to lower imports of minerals and fuels.
The port authority said in a statement that imports fell to 59.8 million tonnes against 65.1 million a year earlier. Seaborne cargo jumped to a record 46.63 million tonnes.
Incoming minerals traffic dropped by more than three million tonnes to 8.3 million. Total minerals cargo fell by 27 percent to 9.5 million tonnes.
Incoming shipments of coal slipped by one million tonnes. Total coal cargo fell by 11.7 percent to 7.7 million tonnes.
The fall was due to the increased use of scrap metal by blast furnaces and high transport prices to the hinterland, it said.
Antwerp remained market leader in Northwest Europe for fruit, steel, paper and cellulose, despite a drop in paper and steel cargo.
Containerised traffic rose by 14 percent, both in tonnage as in TEUs (Twenty foot Equivalent Unit).
"This makes Antwerp the fastest grower of big container ports in the Hamburg-Le Havre range for the third year in a row," the statement said.
Antwerp handled 29.5 million tonnes of containerised goods, which were transported in nearly 1.9 million containers, or 2.65 million TEUs.
Despite the drop in total traffic, more and bigger ships sailed to Antwerp port.
In 1996, 15,417 seaships came to Antwerp, 194 more than in 1995. Their total tonnage rose to some 177.7 million Gross Tonnes (GT) from 167 million a year earlier.
